note: Every modelling choice that is not a sourced observation lives here, so a reader can change one number and re-run.
basis_date_rationale: End of FY2026. The backlog figures are book values as of the close of that fiscal year; the clock accrues forward from there.

escalation.rationale: ENR Construction Cost Index, rounded. Applied to backlog scope held constant, so this component measures only the rising cost of the same work.

identified_by_class.note: Sum of the asset classes that carry a published unfunded dollar figure. Six of eleven classes do.

backlog_basis.conflict_note: Eight figures for the same quantity appear in Berkeley's own documents between 2020 and 2026, ranging from $882M to $2.1B. They are not all measuring the same scope, and no published document reconciles them. This page runs on the $1.8B Auditor-derived point estimate, shows the $1.65-2.5B band around it, and lists the other seven rather than choosing silently.
backlog_basis.unattributed_note: citywide_estimate.point minus identified_by_class.point. Roughly 48% of the headline backlog is not publicly broken out by asset class. This is a finding, not a data error on our side.

published_estimates.source: UC Berkeley CIP studio, from the FY2025-29 CIP
City Auditor financial-condition reporting, as compiled by BeTH
Sum of the asset classes that publish a dollar figure

backlog_basis.comparability_warning: Scope, base year and dollar basis differ across these figures, and several are not dated to a fiscal year. Treat the spread as a measure of how unsettled the number is, not as a trend.

clock_display.rule: A component enters the live rate only when every input it needs carries a source id and a confidence flag. Pending components render as PENDING with the missing input named. Never fold an estimated component into the headline number.
clock_display.seconds_per_year_note: 365.25 * 86400, Julian year, so the rate does not drift across leap years.

separation_rule: Pension/OPEB and deferred capital are rendered as two adjacent tickers and are never summed into a single headline by default. They are different kinds of obligation: one is a legal debt to people, the other a physical debt to assets that can be deferred at a price. A combine toggle exists and states what combining means. As of 2026-08-27 both tickers carry a live rate, and they move in opposite directions - which is the clearest possible argument for not merging them.

bond_debt_service.note: Rate and term are illustrative pending actual bond terms. Used in the overlay to show that a bond is a financing choice, not a funding source.

actuarial_basis_rationale: The balance-sheet date the pension and OPEB net liabilities are carried at. Differs from the capital basis date (2026-06-30) because the two come from different documents; each ticker accrues from its own basis rather than forcing a common one.
